entries.2号航站楼#5b275a3d0244: Before the construction of the capital airport, it was a vast field with dozens of villages scattered. Most of the land in the Qing Dynasty was a royal "fief land", and most of the laborers were nearby villagers. With the downfall of the Qing Dynasty, "fiefdoms" were mostly sold or transferred. In the Republic of China, it was still an open place in northeastern Beijing, a large area of farmland and hills, and ditches were dense.
entries.3号航站楼#10d9e3281b69: Due to the eastern expansion of the capital airport, the land for the new terminal was built. From November 2003 to the end of June 2006, the 6 villages of Longshan, Tahe, Taoshan, Fengjiaying, Unarmed Camp, and Sianma Camp were demolished and relocated within the expansion scope of the airport. More than 6,900 people were relocated to Sanshan Xinxing Homeland, Gangxin Homeland and other residential areas. These villages have a long history. Most of the villages called "battalions" are camps for soldiers and settlers set up in the Ming Dynasty. They have a history of more than 500 years. Renhe Town Tahe Village was founded in Yuan Yanyou for three years (1316), and was named after the river in the west and the tower in the south of the village.
entries.安德里北街#acdc4f01b61b: Andrei got his name from his location between the Doors of Tranquility and the Doors of Desheng. "Beijing Xicheng District Geographical Names" said: "Andri North Street" East-West direction, originally a dirt road, leading to the abandoned Ming Dynasty church, so it is called the Church Street. After 1949, a number of buildings were built on both sides, gradually forming a street. Because there is an Andri residential area not far to the south, it was named Andri North Street. "The street starts from Antingmenwai Street in the east and goes to Ren Ding Lake on the east side of Deshengmenwai Street in the west. In fact, Huang Temple is the historical place name of this region.
entries.安定门#d3e05f8b77c9: According to the "History of Beijing City", Anting Gate was one of the nine gates of Beijing's inner city in the Ming and Qing Dynasties, that is, the eastern gate of Beiyuan. In the first year of Ming Hongwu (1368), after Xu Da led the army to capture the Yuan Metropolis, the wall on the northern side of the metropolis was pushed 5 miles south and rebuilt, and a new gate was built in the place corresponding to Anzhen Gate. It is called "Anting Gate" because it means "to stabilize the world". In the first year of the Ming orthodoxy (1436), we added Antingmen Wengcheng, Jianlou, Zhaolou, etc. The east-west length of the urn city is about 68 meters, the north-south width is about 62 meters, the three-drop water pavilion-style building on the mountain is heavy, the ash cylinder tile green glass tile is trimmed, and the ticket cave gate is a five-volt five-voucher ticket top.
entries.安河桥北#fccbb90e6ec0: At the time of the initial establishment of the subway station, it was called "Longbeicun Station" because of its close proximity to Longbeicun Village, and later renamed "Anheqiao North Station" because of the southern adjacent Anhe Bridge. Longbei Village is close to the Anhe Bridge. Before the Xiaojia River (the western section of the Jinqing River) was cut straight, the adjacent river channel of the village had a curved shape to the north, looking far away and resembling the dragon's back, hence the name. As an ancient village, Anheqiao Village was formed around the Qing Dynasty, and was named after the nearby Anheqiao. During the Republic of China period, it has become a relatively large settlement, including Alley 1 and Alley 2 of Anheqiao West Street, Anheqiao North Hutong, Houhutong, Worship Temple Hutong, etc. In the 1960s and 1970s, it was a village under the jurisdiction of the Qinglongqiao Brigade of the Haidian People's Commune, but it has disappeared and its place name still exists.
entries.安华桥#dccad45b92d9: Built in 1988, Anhua Bridge crosses the North Third Ring Road and is located in the North Central Axis Road, which is named after its proximity to Anhuali. Anhuali is located in the northwest of Chaoyang District, starting from Andingmenwai Street in the east, Xiaohuangzhuang in the east, and Anhuali in the west. The Yuan Dynasty was the western area of the north end of Anzhenmen Street in the Metropolis, and the Qing Dynasty was the outer pavilion and the farmland in the western part of Xiaohuangzhuang. In the early years, many large pits were formed due to soil extraction by kilns. In the summer, there was accumulated water and reeds. There was a large area of farmland nearby. Villagers such as Xiaohuangzhuang mostly cultivated vegetables for their livelihood.
entries.安立路#7f5d8642840f: The Lishui Bridge is an ancient bridge on the ancient road of the Qinghe River. It is said that it was originally a wooden bridge built in the Ming Dynasty. During the Qing Dynasty, a flat girder stone slab bridge was rebuilt on the original site. Because they are made of very hard granite, and there are strong piers standing in the water, they are called "standing water bridges".
entries.安贞门#b721b58e42e5: The location of the northern city of the Yuan Metropolis is still discernible today, that is, from Tucheng north of the Sino-Japanese Friendship Hospital to Tucheng north of the Jimen Bridge. When the Northern Third Ring Road was built in the 1980s, an overpass was built at the intersection of the first and third ring roads of the Anmen Gate and the Anzhenmen Old Site. Because the location of the bridge is on the south side of the Anzhenmen Old Site, it is called "Anzhen Bridge".
entries.奥林匹克公园#4b182bfe66db: The station gets its name from its location in the heart of the Olympic Park. This place was originally under the jurisdiction of Wali Township in Chaoyang District. There are four administrative villages in Wali, Wabian, Kansai Zhuang, and Longwangtang, and the natural villages to which it belonged include North Peak, Leopard House, and Turnoff Exit.
entries.奥体中心#383f300bcd1a: This place was the northern part of Metropolis in the Yuan Dynasty. At that time, it was deserted, and there were scattered people in the Ming and Qing Dynasties. In the Republic of China, it was still an empty place. There was a dirt road that ran from north to south and from east to west. Beiding Village in the north, Cao Bali in the east, Hongmiao Exit on the north side of Beitucheng in the south, Weizikeng Village in the northwest, and Huayanmiao Village in the southwest. It belonged to the seven suburban districts of Beijing. It belonged to the Datun People's Commune in Chaoyang District in the 1960s and 1970s. Due to its flat terrain, there were large areas of rice and vegetables planted. Beichen Road was built in 1986, and its name comes from The Analects of Confucius: "For the sake of government, such as Beichen, the stars (arch) together live in its place.
entries.八宝山#33315789c083: According to "Liao Shi · Han Yanhui Biography" and "Wansha Miscellaneous Records", Han Yanhui (a famous taxi doctor in the Han Dynasty and the Yan people) lived in this mountain, and Han Yanhui and his descendants were buried at the southern foot of this mountain. Therefore, he was named "Han Jiashan", "Hanshan", and later falsely called "Montenegro". In addition, the mountain is also known as "Oven Hill". This name comes from the fact that the peak of Shandong has a stone, which is like an oven; the peak of Shandong has a circular depression, which is similar to an oven. Lingfu Temple was originally built by Haiyun monks from the Yuan Dynasty to the Lunar New Year at the southern foot of Mount Baibao.
entries.八角游乐园#394d13d391e9: Octagon Amusement Park gets its name from its proximity to Octagon Village, which has a long history. According to historical records such as "Wansha Miscellaneous Records" of the Ming Dynasty, Bajiao Village has a history of more than 400 years. According to legend, the ancestors of the villagers were the disaster victims who fled from Hongdong County in Shanxi Province during the Ming Dynasty, and initially settled near Aoshan Mountain (now Laoshan Mountain) to serve as fruit households, vegetable households or raise mules and horses and livestock for the imperial court. Because the first people to migrate were Suo, Guo, Wang, Liang, Zuo, Xiao, Feng, and Zhao, they were called "Eight Villages". Since the accent of Shanxi Hongdong called "Bajia" as "Octagon", "Bajia Village" was homophonously referred to as "Octagon Village".
entries.八里桥#fbfbf9f82796: The "Chronicle of Guangxu Tongzhou" of the Qing Dynasty records: "Yongtong Bridge, built in the 11th year of the Ming Dynasty (1446) in the west of the state city, was named Yongtong. It is now known as the Eight Mile Bridge, five feet east-west, twenty feet north-south, and three holes. When sacrificing liquor and plums, I studied to write a record, and recorded the artistic literature. The Wanli Room was rebuilt, and the Guo Dynasty was repeatedly repaired. In addition, according to" Yongtong Bridge "written by Li Shimian, a sacrificial liquor of the Ming Dynasty," There are rivers in the west of Tongzhou City, and the waters in Kyoto will flow to the east. Although the river is not wide, the rain overflows at the turn of summer and autumn, and often wooden bridges and boats are used as beams.
entries.巴沟#8fbe48c513ba: The name "Wanliu" is derived from falsification, because there are Wanquanzhuang in the south and Liulangzhuang in the north of the area. Wanquanzhuang gets its name from the historical abundance of springs in the area. The name "Wanquanzhuang" first appeared in "Shengzu Imperial System Restoration of the West Top Guangren Palace Monument": "The so-called Wanquanzhuang, Gujiaoji Yishengjing also." In the 1960s and 1970s, Wanquanzhuang was the administrative village of the Haidian People's Commune. Liulangzhuang is today's Liulangzhuang (demolished). According to legend, some people raised cattle here in the Ming Dynasty. It was originally called "Niulanzhuang". Because the willow trees were shaded, it was homophonated as "Liulangzhuang" by the literati inkers, and the story of the Yang family general in the Qing Dynasty was homophonous as "Liulangzhuang".
entries.白堆子#b2c1cf0de7e0: There are various opinions about the origin of the place name "White Heap". It is rumored that when the "five altars and eight temples" of the Beijing City were built, a large amount of stone was needed, most of which was white jiangmi sand (marble), so a special agency for storing and transporting stone was set up outside the Fucheng Gate. Because many white jiangmi sand was piled up, it was commonly known as "white heap". After the agency was revoked, the "white heap" was retained as a place name.
entries.白石桥南#f3bf579f1d68: There are two ways to say the name "Four Paths". According to legend, during the Ming and Qing Dynasties, two ancient roads intersected here, one was southeast and northwest, from the Three Pagodas Temple to the Baishi Bridge; the other was east-west, from the Huangtu Pit outside the Xizhimen Gate to Xibali Zhuang. There is a water well on the northeast side of the entrance, and a tea house with a surname of Chang opened next to the well. Although the facade is small, the merchants who travel between the four crossings in the southeast and northwest are more frequent, and gradually form settlements. According to the name of the crossing, "Four Crossings". In addition, the name "Sidaokou" is related to the "Jingmen Railway" (also known as the "Jingmen Branch Line") built at the end of the Qing Dynasty.
entries.百子湾#9f88ea6ba6f4: "Chaoyang District, Beijing" contains: Baiziwan "The village name is rumored to have come from three sources: from Gaobeidian to Dongbianmen there was a dirt road, winding like a snake, and the curve was close to a hundred places, so it was called Baiziwan; Baiziwan was once known as Baiziwan, which was later disgusting, and the homonym was" Baiziwan "; it was originally a low-lying land, only tares can be planted, so it has the name of" Laiziwan ". It was established in 1948."
entries.北安河#c9202ba0c1bf: "Beijing Haidian District Geographical Names" said: The village "was originally called Bei 'anwo, the monument of Xingshan Temple is engraved with the name of Anhe, and the later homonym is the current name. According to" The Old News of the Sun ": ‘Ten miles out of Baiwang (now Baiwang Mountain) is the Changle River, and the river is not broad and flows. The Changle River is the Anhe River, and its land has Nanan River, Bei 'an River... villages. It is also said that the place used to be called" An 'an ", which was originally just a small village." An 'an "refers to the residence where people live or gather. In the Ming Dynasty, the settlements increased, and the villagers were mostly concentrated in the south and north of the village, which was gradually divided into two villages, called" Beianhe "and" Nananhe ", and the later homonyms were" Beianhe "and" Nananhe ".
entries.北工大西门#5b99acf1a501: In the early years, this area was mostly farmland and mass graves, of which Hauge Tomb was the largest. Aishinjoro Haug was the eldest son of Tai Chi, the emperor of the Qing Dynasty. He was first promoted to Baylor, and promoted to Tensatsu in 1632. In the first year of Zunde (1636), Prince Su was sealed with meritorious service, which was reduced to Baylor in the year of the event, and Prince Su was sealed again the following year. In the sixth year of Zongde (1641), he was demoted to the county king, and in the following year, he was reappointed as the prince of Su. In the first year of Junji (1644), the relationship was cut. Shunzhi five years (1648) was framed by the regent Dorje and committed suicide in captivity. In the seventh year of the reign of Shunzhi (1650), the snow was blown out and Prince Suu was recovered.
entries.北宫门#c853873f9c66: Entering the Beigong Gate is the back mountain of Yiheyuan Wanshou Mountain, and there are many buildings in the early years. Among them, Suzhou Street was built to imitate Jiangnan Water Town, commonly known as "Buy and Sell Street". During the Qingyiyuan period, there were various shops on the shore, such as jade antique shops, satin shops, snack shops, tea houses, gold and silver jewelry buildings, etc. The guys in the store were all dressed as eunuchs and palace ladies. The emperor started "business" when he was lucky. Dozens of shops on the shores of the back lake were burned down by the Great Powers in 1860. The current landscape was rebuilt in 1986 and is the main scenic spot of Yiheyuan Houshan. The Beigong Gate is the northern gate of the Summer Palace, one of the "three mountains and five gardens". It was built during the Qianlong period. It was formerly known as the "Beilou Gate". After being rebuilt during the Guangxu period, it was renamed the "Beigong Gate".
entries.北海北#56a727ceb6dd: After the Revolution of 1911, the Beihai Sea was once occupied by warlords, and Yuan Shikai temporarily lived in Jingxinzhai. In August 1925, the park was opened to the public. There are many sceneries in the park, such as Yong 'an Temple, Falun Hall, Yuexin Temple, Qingxiao Tower, Kowloon Wall, Dragon Pavilion, Jingxinzhai, etc. The Tibetan-style white tower on Qionghua Island is one of the iconic buildings in Beijing. The stone tablet entitled "Qiongdao Chunyin" by the Emperor Qianlong stands in the depths of the green shade and is one of the "Eight Scenes of Yanjing".
entries.北京南站#0ebba671fb21: Beijing South Railway Station is located in the ancient village of Pengzhuang. Before 1949, there were dozens of acres of vegetable fields. Initially, there were only two families, Peng and Jia. It is said that they fled from Shandong during the Qianlong period of the Qing Dynasty. They made their home here. Because Peng was a big family and lived here for a long time, they were called "Pengzhuang". In addition to vegetable fields, there were many cemeteries and large reed ponds nearby, a small road leading to the Yongding Gate in the northeast. After 1949, the cemeteries and large reed ponds in this area were levelled and many residents' houses were built. After the construction of the Yongding Gate railway station in 1957, the name "Pengzhuang" was gradually faded, but it is still used as a place name and now belongs to the Pengzhuang community of Yongwai Street.
entries.北京西站#550bf59eb63a: The idea of building Beijing West Railway Station began as early as 1959, and was planned and studied three times in history, but was shelved for various reasons. In the early 1990s, in order to ease the tension of Beijing Station operation, Beijing West Railway Station was finally built here, and completed in early 1996. It was the largest modern railway passenger station in Asia.
entries.北京站#b2b922ad2535: Beijing Station dates back to the 27th year of Qing Guangxu (1901). The original site is located on the east side of Zhengyangmen Urn City. It was built in 1901 and completed in the 29th year of Guangxu (1903). It was formerly known as "Zhengyangmen East Station of the Jingfeng Railway". Historically, it has used the names of Qianmen Station, Beijing Station, Beiping Station, Beiping East Station, etc. It has been renamed "Beijing Station" since September 30, 1949. After 1949, the passenger traffic of the original station has increased, far from meeting the passenger transportation requirements, so it was decided to build a new station at a different address. On January 20, 1959, the new Beijing Station was officially built in the southeast of today's Dongcheng District.
entries.北沙滩#09e7ea40086b: Separately, when the Ming Dynasty built the Beijing City, it dug sand here, thus forming a number of large sand pits, two or three miles long from north to south. Whenever the wind blows, the yellow sand rises, so the population is sparse and very desolate, commonly known as the "beach pit". After heavy rains every summer, it turns into a large pond full of reeds, known as a "reed pit". Around the early Qing Dynasty, people settled here, gradually reclaimed the land nearby, and formed a village, which was named "Beach Village" because of its sandy soil. The late Republic of China developed into two natural villages in the north and south, called "South Beach" and "North Beach" respectively.
entries.北邵洼#147e03626134: When the subway station was originally set up here, it was called "Changping New District Station" because it was located in the Changping New District under planning and construction. Later, it was renamed because of its proximity to Beishaowa Village. "Geographical Names of Changping County, Beijing" contains: "Beishaowa became a village in the Ming Dynasty, set up a military settlement in the early Ming Dynasty, called Beishaotun, later evolved into today's name". According to "Changping Town and Village Tianyuan", "Beishaowa is opposite to Nanshao (sentry), and the meaning is similar. The place has built an outpost just north of the camp area, so it is called Beishaotun (sentry). As for why it is also called Beishao (Sentinel) Wa, this is mainly because the terrain of the area is indeed low-lying compared with the surrounding area, especially compared with the small North Sentinel near the east of the village, the elevation of the village site is 3.1 meters different.
entries.北土城#a89b0b29245d: When the subway station was first set up here, it was called "Panda Ring Island Station". Since the panda was selected as the mascot of the 11th Asian Games in 1990, a Hanbai jade panda sculpture was set up outside the Asian Games Village at that time, that is, in the ring island where Beichen Road and Beitucheng Road intersected, which was popularly known as "Panda Ring Island". In April 2005, the panda sculpture was removed due to the construction of the subway station. The walls of the Yuan Metropolis were built in 1267 and basically completed in 1276. Because it is all made of rammed earth, the base is about 24 meters wide, the top is about 8 meters wide, and the height is about 16 meters, so it is called "Tucheng".
entries.北新桥#2c76e34677d7: In the Yuan Dynasty, today's Beixinqiao area was called "Xingqiao", in the Ming Dynasty it was called "Fleece Household Corner", and during the Qing Dynasty it was renamed "Beixinqiao". There is also a popular story about the origin of this place name.
entries.北苑#63e4b9f3bc55: Beiyuan was named for its location on the northern outskirts of Beijing. As early as the Yuan Dynasty, this area was densely forested with grass for dozens of miles. The royals sent people here to build a palace for their emperors to hunt, raising a large number of deer, catfish and other animals. Every spring and autumn, emperors come here to hunt. The ancestors of Beiyuan were Han people who provided services for the Beiyuan hunting ground, and gradually gathered to become Beiyuan Village. In ancient China, "Yuan", also known as "Bian", originally referred to a place with beautiful water grasses and lush forests, suitable for raising animals, and later became a royal garden for emperors to play shooting and hunting.
entries.北苑路北#cd288fb485fb: Since the Yuan Dynasty, beef and mutton and beef and mutton products have increasingly become indispensable in the lives of the people of Beijing. There are many mutton shops on the streets of Beijing, so there is a great demand for mutton, and most of them are in the "sheep shop" and "sheep shop" in northern Beijing. With the increase in the number of "sheepfolds" and "sheepfold shops" in this area for a long time, a large-scale trading market for live sheep and sheep meat products has been formed, commonly known as "big sheep shop", or "big sheep shop" for short. Later, a large village was formed, called "Yangfang Village", but most people call it "Big Goat Square", which is still used today.
entries.北运河东#0ee84cd5b511: There are many villages along the North Canal. The subway station on the east side of the North Canal is close to Yangtuo Village, so when the subway station was first set up, it was called "Yangtuo Station". "Geographical Names of Tongxian County, Beijing" records: Yang Tuo Chengcun of the Ming Dynasty, but the family that originally settled here was not surnamed Yang, but surnamed Zhou. They built the village on top of Tu Tuo, so their name was "Zhou Jiatuo". Tuo is a long earthen pit shaped like a serpentine twist. In the early Qing Dynasty, people surnamed Yang settled nearby, forming a settlement called "Yang Jiatuo". Due to the rapid development of Yangjiatuo, the scale of the village greatly exceeded that of Zhoujiatuo, and the two villages were basically connected. In the Republic of China, the second village was also called "Yangjiatuo", later referred to as "Yangjiatuo".
entries.北运河西#df67a55bdae7: When the subway station was first set up, it was called "Yudaihe Street Station" because it was located in the eastern section of Yudaihe East Street, and later it was named "North Canal West Station" because it was adjacent to the North Canal to the east.
entries.菜市口#9cffa48c256e: The main reason for the popularity of the culinary market entrance was that the Qing government moved the execution ground for homicide from the West Fourth Building (then called West City) in the Ming Dynasty to the culinary market entrance outside Xuanwumen. It is said that the execution ground of that year was located near the intersection on the north side of Caishikou Street today. The "Beiping Travel Guide" compiled by Ma Zhiying contains: Every time the court trial is held after autumn, when there are many prisoners executed in Beijing, it is arranged from east to west, and the executioner is executed from east to west with a knife in hand. Thus, "Cai Shikou" has become a synonym of "execution venue". The high seat of the supervisor at the time of the beheading is often located in front of the store of the old brand "Xihe Nian Tang".
entries.草房#d7d558f86d11: The name "grass house" is related to the storage of forage in the imperial horse farm set up in northwest Tongzhou in the Ming Dynasty. According to legend, during the Jiajing period, the Ministry of Housing set up a horse ranch in the eastern three miles of the land, and the grass house was attached to the horse ranch. Located in the eastern part of Beijing, it is sparsely populated and mostly empty, with green grass every summer.
entries.草桥#9e138e6733c2: The Ma Cao River is a major river in Fengtai, originating from Fanjiacun. It flows from west to east, and enters the Liangshui River through Yuquanying, Caoqiao, and Majiabao. Historically, it has had abundant water, providing a rich source of water for flowers and trees along the coast. When the rainy season came, the water of the Ma Cao River soared, causing many inconveniences for people to travel. In the Ming Dynasty, a wooden bridge was built on the river. In the Qing Dynasty, it was changed to a slate bridge. Because it crossed the Ma Cao River, it was called a "grass bridge". There is a village on the east side of the river, which is named because of its proximity to the grass bridge.
entries.茶棚#36145f8f0a43: Miaofeng Mountain is located in northwest Beijing, and its peak, Bixia Yuanjun Temple, is commonly known as the "Maiden Temple". During the Ming and Qing Dynasties and the Republic of China, it was a famous holy place. There are temple festivals from the first to the fifteenth of April every year, and many people go to the Golden Peak of Myofeng Mountain to worship. The people in the capital came out of Xizhimen, Fuchengmen, and Xibenmen, and headed northwest to Liulangzhuang, through the Blue Indigo Factory, South Dock, and North Dock to the bottom of Yuquan Mountain, then through the Kungde Temple and Qinglong Bridge, over the Hongshan Pass, then crossed the Northwest Wang and Hot Spring to the Bei 'an River to the northwest, then turned into the direction of Miaofeng Mountain, and along the Xiangdao to the Jindingniangniangmiao. The tea shed under Jade Spring Mountain is a must for many perfumers to go to Mt. Myohoen and Mt. Xiangshan.
entries.昌平#14c5af6a0a7d: Changping is a western Hanzhi County, originally belonging to the same Shanggu County as Jundu County. From the Western Han Dynasty to the beginning of the Northern Wei Dynasty, its city site is located in the southeast of the current site, on the north bank of the Wenyu River (in the Xinlitun Village area of the present-day Shahe Town). In the beginning of the Northern Wei Dynasty, Changping County was abolished to enter Junzhi County. During the Tianping period of the Eastern Wei Dynasty, Changping County was resettled and belonged to Pyeongchang County. The county was rebuilt in the old city of the original Junzhi County, which was founded at the end of the Warring States Period, and is located in the southwest of the current site (in the Tucheng Village area of the present-day Ma Chikou Town). About the middle age of the Tang Dynasty, Changping County was also relocated to the area of the old county village eight miles west of the present site, and built the city known as Bai Futu City.
entries.昌平东关#1823a3d87e69: The historic Dongguan site of Changping City is roughly at the intersection of Donghuan Road and Gulou East Street in Changping City today, rather than the location of Changping Dongguan Metro Station. The so-called Dongguan is actually the east gate of Yongan City.
entries.昌平西山口#7bb8fb8e76d0: The historical West Pass is one of the ten passes of the Ming Tombs, named after its relative position.
entries.常营#eb2b350d0d42: Changying has a long history as one of the gathering places for Hui residents in Beijing. At the beginning of the Ming Dynasty, the general Chang Yuchun (Hui Min) conquered the capital of Yuan from Xu Da Bei, and in 1369, in order to resist the generals of the Yuan Dynasty and quickly invade Tongzhou, he set up a camp here. Since then, a group of Hui people's army led by Chang Yuchun has been stationed here for a long time to form a village. Because the villagers are mostly descendants of the Chang clan, they are called "Changjiayingzi", later called "Changying" and "Changying".
entries.朝阳公园#4bbe25a33672: According to legend, in the Qing Dynasty, the royal family issued "eight banners of rice" here, and used the water in a nearby lake as a driving force to shell the rice with a water husk, so it got the place name of "water husk". In the early years, the western part of Shuiweizi Village was a famous pottery kiln in Beijing. For a long time, pottery pots were fired, and kiln pits, lake ponds, and reeds were formed due to soil collection. It was commonly known as "reed pit". A larger reed pit is called "Shuiweizi Lake" near Shuiweizi Village, and there is a large area of farmland nearby. In the 1950s, a residential area was built nearby, which was named "Shuiweizi Dongli" and "Shuiweizi Xili" according to the name of "Shuiweizi".
entries.朝阳门#0a54bddf1ca8: Chaoyangmen was one of the nine gates of the inner city of Beijing in the Ming and Qing Dynasties. "Shuntianfu Chronicle" records: In the fourth year of the Yuan Dynasty (1267), Kublai Khan ordered "the construction of a new city, 60 miles from the city... 11 gates... on the right side of the east, and on the left side of the east, Guangxi...". The "Qihua Gate" located on the right side of the east is today's Chaoyangmen. The word "unification" comes from "I Ching · Gossip", "Qi Ye, the cleanness of all things".
entries.车道沟#861a0fe2c0f4: According to "Jade Spring Mountain Lower Seasons", there are two sources for the Dao Ditch. It is said that this place is located outside the Xizhimen Gate. In the early years, the carmadeau from Beijing to the west passed by here. For a long time, the originally flat avenue was crushed by the car to create a deep ditch of many widths, commonly known as the "lane ditch". In addition, there was a river ditch in this place, which was the tributary of the long river. Later, the tributary dried up, forming a low-lying earth road. Sometimes there were carriages and horses passing by, so it was called "lane ditch". There is a village not far to the east of this place. Because it is close to the lane ditch, it is called "Lane Ditch Village".
entries.车公庄#8ee59a7e6406: The location of the station is actually the Guanyuan Bridge on the West Second Ring Road, which is named after the adjacent Guanyuan on the east side. Guanyuan, formerly known as Guayuan, is related to the Chaotian Palace in the Ming Dynasty. Chaotian Palace was built in the Yuan Dynasty as the Heavenly Master's Palace. In 1433, it was rebuilt after the Nanjing Chaotian Palace. It is located in the northwest of Baita Temple. Inside, there is a Dorokushi to teach the Taoism of the Lord and the Kingdom of Heaven. It is also the place for the ceremonies of the hundreds of official exercises. The Chaotian Palace is huge in scale, reaching Funei Street in the south, the official park in the north, the Fusui Boundary in the west, the Emerald Flower Crossing Hutong in the east, and the Gongmen Gate in the west of today's Gongmen Gate.
entries.车公庄西#fe3df85b1d16: The exhibition hall road runs north-south, and is named after the Beijing Exhibition Hall at its northern end. The Beijing Exhibition Hall was built in 1953 to hold an exhibition on Soviet industrial and agricultural production and to introduce the achievements of Soviet culture and education. A large-scale exhibition hall jointly designed and built by Soviet experts and Chinese technicians was completed in September 1954. It was originally known as the "Beijing Soviet Exhibition Hall" and renamed the "Beijing Exhibition Hall" after 1958.
entries.成寿寺#811e636a940b: The "Beijing Temple Historical Data", known as the "Beijing Temple Comprehensive", contains the basic information of more than 1,500 temples in and around the capital city, including a "Chengshou Temple", but "It is located at No. 19 Chunshu Hutong in Dengshikou, Inner District, and was built in the first year of Chenghua in the Ming Dynasty, which is a private building". The "Temple Registration of the Beiping Special Municipal Government" in 1928 and the "First General Registration of the Temple of the Beiping Municipal Government" in 1936 are recorded for this temple, but there is no record of the Chengshou Temple in Beijing Nanfengtai. The "Geographical Names of Fengtai District, Beijing" said: "The original temple was named Chengshou Temple, so this is the name of the village.
entries.崇文门#81555b83505e: Chongwenmen is the city gate with the most names among Beijing's old city gates. During the Ming and Qing Dynasties, because it was a dedicated channel for transporting wine to the Imperial City, it was called the "wine gate", and it was also the gate for talented people to enter Beijing to catch up with the examination. Ya called it the "gate of luck". In the Ming Dynasty, the "Beijing Teacher Taxation Office" was located on the east of the main street outside Chongwenmen Street. The Qing Dynasty continued to use the old system of the Ming Dynasty, and still set up a "Supervision Office" to collect taxes on goods, so it was also called "tax gate".
entries.传媒大学#8bdc8684b3ff: What is "Yanzi Well"? That is, a place that is convenient for passers-by to drink water in the early years. In the era when there were no bicycles or cars, in addition to rich people riding cars and horses, the vast majority of ordinary people used walking to replace cars. At that time, the underground water level in the suburbs of Beijing was very shallow, and the water surface in the well was only three or four feet from the ground. It was desirable to bend over, and there were many trees near the well. In order to relieve the thirst of past passers-by, some benefactors hang a wooden spoon to draw water - commonly known as a "scoop" - on the tree. Passers-by come here thirsty, take off the scoop, go to the well to draw water to drink, and then hang it on the tree after use.
entries.慈寿寺#51971985ca46: In addition to court funding, princes, princesses, eunuchs, etc. also contributed to the construction of the temple, demonstrating the royal importance and admiration for Buddhism. Cishouji Temple was abandoned during the Qing Dynasty, and there was no way to record the reason. It is said that a fire in the Qing Dynasty burned down all the buildings in the temple, leaving only one brick tower, the Linglong Pagoda, commonly known as the "Eight Mile Pagoda", which is now located in the Exquisite Park of Ba Li Zhuang in the west of Beijing. Cishouji Temple, also known as Yong 'an Temple, was built in the fourth year of the Ming Wanli calendar (1576). It was selected by the Empress Dowager Cixi, the birth mother of the Emperor Wanli of the Myeongshen Sect, to preside over the construction.
entries.磁器口#7fc03a98634b: The history of the magnet port can be traced back to the Yuan Dynasty, when it was located outside the Civilization Gate (Chongwen Gate), which was the only way to enter the city in the southeast of the Yuan Metropolis. Due to the frequent exchanges of personnel, some people set up stalls outside the city gate to sell, of which garlic is mostly operated, so it is called "garlic city". After the construction of Beijing's outer city during the Jiajing period of the Ming Dynasty, this area became a city. From the period from Wanli to the Chonglong period and the Qianlong period of the Qing Dynasty, it was called "Garlic Market". After forming a street heading north and south, it was called "Garlic Market Street".
entries.次渠#6a31e5c4c2be: There is a Baoguang Temple, also known as Fahua Temple, commonly known as the cone tower in Jiqu Village. In the early years, there was a folk saying in the southwest of Tongzhou, "Tongzhou's tower, the cone of the secondary channel, and the king's eight-pack stone tablet of Majuqiao." This "cone of the secondary channel" refers to the cone tower in the Baoguang Temple of the secondary channel. The temple was built in the first year of the Yuan Dynasty (1297), and in the five years of the Ming Orthodoxy (1440), the Zhibaoguang Zen Temple was granted. The bronze bell hangs in the temple, and the bell is cast with "Da Ming Jing Tai". The voice is round, deep, and long. It can be transmitted for more than ten miles, which is rare in Beijing city.
entries.次渠南#e3aa9caeb9e3: The station is named because of its location in the southern part of Subqua Town and the southwestern part of Subqua Station, which is close to the historical Cui Jia Kiln. "Beijing Tongxian Geographical Names" records: "In the 15th year of Qianlong in the Qing Dynasty (1750), Cui surnamed came to this place to operate brick kilns as an industry, and gradually formed settlements after 1913, hence the name."
entries.崔各庄#62de105b8f56: After the establishment of the Ming Dynasty, in order to consolidate the border defense in the north, a large number of people were expropriated from Shanxi, Shandong and the south to Beijing and the surrounding areas today. Every time the expropriation population was tens of thousands of households, these people who came from afar lived in groups with the same family, the same surname and the same township, and named the new place of residence after the surname of the original settlers. Therefore, many place names such as "Zhangjiazhuang" and "Wangjiazhuang" appeared. At that time, the immigrants in the Cui Gezhuang area were southerners, so they were called "Cui Jiazhuang", which later evolved into "Cui Gezhuang".
entries.褡裢坡#1ed414a7693a: "Geographical Names of Chaoyang District, Beijing" records: "Huangqu Village borders Huangqu Village in the east, Baijialou in the west, Dingfuzhuang in the south, and Shigezhuang in the north. Originally it was the cemetery of the Jiang clan. After becoming a village, it was settled on a high slope and resembled a hillside. Therefore, it was named". What is a "puppy"? That is, a kind of cloth pocket used by the elderly, with an opening in the middle and things at both ends. When they travel, they put them on their shoulders and store some small items. Commonly known as "bags", the local name is also known as "money forks". Shanxi, Hebei and other places have this name.
entries.达官营#966870304548: The name of "Da Guan Battalion" has many sayings. Second, the official battalion was related to the ancient garrison. "Daguan" is another name for "Takan". According to legend, the Yuan Army, or Mongol army, was stationed here during the Yuan Dynasty, when the Han called the Mongols "Tatars." After Kublai Khan in Beijing Dingdu, a large number of Mongolian troops were stationed in and around the metropolis, which the Han people called "Tazi". Today, there is a Mongolian military camp in the area of Daguan Battalion, so it is called "Tazi Battalion" and "Taguan Battalion", later changed to "Daguan Battalion".
entries.大葆台#b2f5427ec6e2: Dabaotai is famous for the excavation of the Western Han tomb of Dabaotai in 1974. Previously, "Dabaotai" was just a little-known place.
entries.大红门#c750f6781b74: According to "Daxing Wenhistory": Dahongmen was originally the main gate of the Imperial Court Nanhaizi, which was built in the 12th year of Yongle Ming Dynasty (1414). At the time of the expansion of Nanhaizi, one door was opened in each of the four directions, namely, "Donghongmen", "Xihongmen", "Nanhongmen" and "Beihongmen", of which the North Hongmen was the main gate of Nanyuan. Five more gates were opened during the Qianlong period of the Qing Dynasty. A gate built east of the North Hongmen was called the "Little Hongmen". Therefore, the original North Hongmen was also called the "North Great Hongmen". Because it was the most convenient gate for the emperor to enter and exit, it was the most regulated gate in the "Nanhaizi", so it was called the "Great Hongmen".
entries.大红门南#c3fb5feae721: Dahongmen was the main gate of Nanhaizi in the Imperial Garden during the Ming and Qing Dynasties. This place is located in the inner part of Dahongmen. The ruins of the Republic of China still exist, with a large area of farmland, a number of scattered settlements nearby, and a yellow pavilion. It is the site of the tomb of Fu Zifan, a doctor of Guanglu in the Qing Dynasty, and was built in the eighth year of the Republic of China (1919). The pavilion is four corners, the top is covered with yellow glazed tiles, about 3 meters high, and there is a stone monument in the center, two dragons are carved on both sides of the monument, which is a famous landscape around the Great Hongmen.
entries.大郊亭#a82d494de030: It is recorded in the literature that as early as the Liao Dynasty, the area around the Great Suburban Pavilion was once a large area of shallow water lakes, which was called "suburban lake". At that time, the capital of the Liao state was called "Shangjing", which was in the south of the left flag of Cuba Lin in Inner Mongolia today. At that time, Beijing called "Yanjing" (also known as "Nanjing"), which was the capital of the Liao state. "Jiudian" is located in the northeast of Yenching, less than 100 miles away. In the sixth year of the Taiping Dynasty (1026), a prince went hunting in the eastern suburbs of Yenching. When he came to the area of today's big suburban pavilion, he saw that it was dense with water and grass, and wild ducks and wild birds flocked. He was very happy. In just half a day, he fought more than a dozen wild ducks, and when he left, he said that he would come here to hunt in the future.
entries.大井#80d870004984: "Beijing Fengtai District Geographical Names" said: "Daijing was originally called Yijing or Honey Well. According to the Qing Dynasty's" Sunshine Old News Examination "," Gi Jing 'an is ten miles west of Guang 'an Gate. "’It is also said that the" Chang 'an Guest Story "contains:‘ Yi Well or Honey Well, it is said that Wen Huang (Yongle) is stationed in Ganqiquan, hence the name. ’" According to legend, one spring, Emperor Yongle went to Yunju Temple in Fangshan to enjoy the scenery. When he passed by Ooi Village, he stopped and rested.
entries.大石河东#721a936918d0: The station gets its name from its location on the east side of the Dashi River. Dashihe is the longest river in Fangshan District, running through the north and south of the district. According to the "History of Fangshan", the Dashi River is a tributary of the North Juma River in the Daqing River Basin, which originated in the northwest of Xiayunling Township in the western mountainous region of China. The river twists and turns eastward between the valleys, passing through Xiayunling, Changgong, Banggezhuang, Hebei and other places, and exits the mountain in Tulixin Kaikou Village... to Ancestral Village and exits to the south, to the Jiuzhou City Wharf Town in Hebei Province and the North Juma River, with a total length of 129 kilometers, including 108 kilometers in Fangshan District.
entries.大屯路东#8d8219b162cd: As a village in the northern part of the capital city, Datun first appeared in the "Sunshine Old News" in the Qing Dynasty, which has records of "Datun Village Yong 'an Zhuang Zhenwu Temple" and "Datun Village is north of Tuguan". The name of Datun began in the Southern Song Dynasty. There is a record in the Chaoyang District Geographical Names Chronicle of Beijing that "Datun Village used to be called Yonganzhuang, and it was rumored that the Southern Song Dynasty was the land of grain", but this is questioned by historians, because the jurisdiction of the Southern Song Dynasty can not reach today's Beijing, it may be the land of Jin Guotun soldiers, but there is no historical record. Second, the name of Datun began in the Ming Dynasty.
entries.大瓦窑#104103f61b53: "Geographical Names of Fengtai District, Beijing" contains: "It is said that when the city of Beijing was built, the kiln was burned here, hence the name Dawa Kiln Village." Fengtai Place Name Detective "said:" Wansha Miscellaneous Records "records that there is" Wa Kiln Head "in the area south of Ba Li Zhuang outside the Fucheng Gate." Guang Xu Shun Tian Fu Chi "said that" Thirty-six Li Wa Kiln Village, Shuitun, Lugu Village, Zhang Yi Village, Thirty-seven Li North Wa Kiln... The above villages are in the east of Yongding River "to the west of Wanping County. The" Wa Yaotou "and" Wa Yao Village "here are the" Xiaowa Kiln "located 5 kilometers northwest of Lugouqiao Township today. The history of the village can be traced back to the Ming Dynasty.
entries.大望路#8826ee047dc1: This station is named after its location in the northern section of West Dawang Road. Xidawang Road is a sub-road of the city heading north and south. It starts from Chaoyang Road in the north and goes south to Songyu South Road. It has been mentioned in the "Beiping City Map" in 1947 (1947). At that time, the southern end only reached Shaban Street (now Nanmofang Road). It is said that Xidawang Road was originally called "Xidawang Road", which was named after Wang's family living nearby in the early years, and later evolved into "Xidawang Road". In 1965, it was renamed "Guanghui Road" because of the Beijing Thermal Power Plant on the east side of the northern section of the road, and was restored to its current name in 1979. Speaking of Xidawang Road, one of the most familiar place names in Beijing: Bawang Tomb.
entries.大兴机场#f1043dca4ff5: According to "Guangyang History", the name "Guangyang" originated from Guangyang County established during the Warring States Period, Qin Dynasty, and Eastern Han Dynasty, which has a history of more than 2,000 years. Kyushu Town is under the jurisdiction of Guangyang District, 11 km from Langfang Downtown. Daxing Airport Station is located between Kyushu Zhentuan Chengcun and Tuancheng Xinzhuang. According to the "Chronicle of Guangyang District, Langfang City", during the Jintianhui period, the area around Jiuzhou Town (Old State) in Guangyang District today belonged to the Seikin Prefecture on Yenching Road and was a major town in Beijing. In order to strengthen the defense, several castles, commonly known as regimental cities, were built in the areas under the jurisdiction of the old state.
entries.大兴新城#0d0004f1b7cf: The name "Daxing" has a long history. Qin Dynasty Jian County was named after the Yuan Dynasty. The earliest was Guji County, which was named because it was built in the Jicheng area and was built in the Spring and Autumn Period and the Warring States Period. Twenty-three years after Qin Shihuang (224 BC), the Imperial Court was "located in Guangyang County and Jixian County" in the Jicheng area. Since the Han Dynasty to the Sui and Tang Dynasties and the Five Dynasties, the system of Ji County has always existed. In the first year of the Liao Hui (938 AD), Ji County was renamed Jibei County and belonged to Yudu Prefecture. In the first year of Liao Kaitai (1012), Jibei County was renamed Seijin County and belonged to Seijin Prefecture. After Yenching, the capital of Jinqian, was renamed Zhongdu, and the Jin Prefecture was renamed Yong 'an Prefecture.
entries.大钟寺#1fbbcbbbf588: After Ming Chengzu Zhu Di moved to Beijing, he minted a large bronze bell with a height of 6.94 meters, an outer diameter of 3.3 meters, and a weight of 46.5 tons. The inner wall of the bell has more than 100 Buddhist sutras and spells, a total of more than 230,000 characters, composed of Han and Sanskrit. It is called "Yongle Bell" because it was cast in the 19th year of Yongle (1421). During the Ten Thousand Years period, this large bell was moved to Wanshou Temple in the western suburbs, and six monks struck the bell every day. During the Yongzheng era of the Qing Dynasty, some people said that it was unlucky to put bells in Wanshou Temple. Every day, they saw bells (the end) and heard bells (the end). How can they "live forever"?
entries.稻田#1048c4f7b6e7: The "Geographical Names of Fangshan District in Beijing" contains: "The rice field became a village before the Ming Dynasty, because it is located on the banks of the Yongding River, the south of the village is a lowland, the terrain is low and flat, irrigation is convenient, and the history of rice cultivation is long, which is why it got its name." It is rumored that in the early Ming Dynasty, a general surnamed Wang who followed Zhu Yuanzhang to beat the whole world was far-sighted and foresaw that Zhu Yuanzhang would slaughter distinguished officials after he ascended the throne, so he took the initiative to resign north after the founding of the Ming Dynasty and live in Metropolis.
entries.稻香湖路#4dad1f4c485b: This place is adjacent to Sanxingzhuang in the north, and Chengcun in the early Qing Dynasty. According to legend, there are three adjacent wells in the village, which are distributed in a three-star shape, so they are called "Sanjingzhuang" or "Sanxingzhuang". In addition, there were three families in the initial settlement, called "Sanzhuang", and the later homonym was "Sanxingzhuang". "Qingguangxu Shuntianfu Chronicle" is recorded as "Sanxingzhuang". It belonged to the Sujiatuo People's Commune in Haidian District in the 1960s and 1970s. At that time, rice cultivation area accounted for more than half of the cultivated land, and villagers were mostly engaged in rice cultivation.
entries.德茂#c6dba42cc914: This station is named after its location in Demaochuang. According to the "Geographical Names of Daxing County in Beijing": "In 1902, Nanyuan was abandoned in the 28th year of the Qing Dynasty (1902). The official approved the recruitment of Tuotunen. This place became a landlord's manor, named Demaozhuang, which was once Shuntianfu Daxing County, and was once known as‘ Eight Families’."
entries.灯市口#3f446a5b565d: The origin of the lantern market can be traced back to the Ming Dynasty. During the Yongle period, in today's Dengshikou Avenue, a commercial street was formed, shops gathered, and the noise was extraordinary. Every year from the eighth to the eighteenth day of the first lunar month, the shops and restaurants here each hang colorful lights. From the hustle and bustle of the market during the day, it suddenly turns into a dazzling street of lights. Among them, the lights on this day of the Yuan Festival are the most abundant. Therefore, there is a saying that "the fourteenth day to test the lights, the fifteenth day to test the lights, and the sixteenth day to strike the lights". The name of the "Lantern Market" is derived from the Lantern Market.
entries.东大桥#8ef40e21f662: According to "Chaoyang Literary History", in the early years, today's workers' stadium was a pond depression, and a drainage ditch flowed south from the pond along the west side of Jin Gongti East Road, to Chaoyang Gate just outside the city gate and east. In order to facilitate transportation, a wooden bridge was built here in the Ming Dynasty. At the end of the Qing Dynasty, it was changed to a stone bridge. The bridge body was not tall, more than 60 meters long, and more than 13 meters wide (the bridge was more than ten meters long and more than three meters wide). The bridge deck was paved with tiger and leather stones, and the bridge railing was inlaid with granite. The workmanship was exquisite. Because it is located on the east side of the Chaoyang Gate, commonly known as the "East Bridge", its general location is at the boundary between the motor lane and the non-motor lane opposite the north of the East Road of the Jianlan Island Building.
entries.东单#83b33f0f24af: During the Ming orthodox year, at the south end of the Dongdan intersection today, that is, on the east side of the Dongdan Stadium, a four-pillar three-floor wooden building was built. Because the plaque was inscribed with the word "", it was called "". "Just as the Sun" is taken from "Just as the Sun, Looking Like a Cloud" in the History of the Five Emperors, which means watching the sunrise (looking at the clouds in the west) from the east. Fan Zhongyun's "Ming Tangfu" also has the phrase "look forward to the clouds and the sun, and sing praises to Shun". The building is located in the east of the Imperial City and is a single-seat building, commonly known as "Dongdan Building", or "Dongdan" for short.
entries.东风北桥#3517d757e2d5: The station is named for its proximity to the Dongfeng North Bridge in the southeast, and the "Dongfeng" originates from the "Dongfeng Farm" that once existed.
entries.东高地#fc33a3ef143f: In the early years, the area was hilly and roughly low-lying in the west and higher in the east. There is a large area of wetlands in the west. Every midsummer, reed grass is overgrown, while there are many high hills in the east. There is a large flat area between the two, because it is triangular, commonly known as "triangular land". In the Republic of China, this area has been reclaimed a lot of farmland. In the early 1950s, it had formed a large settlement, belonging to Nanyuan District, Beijing. In 1954, it was transferred to Nanyuan Town Office. In 1958, Nanyuan District was abolished, and the jurisdiction of Nanyuan Town Office was merged into Fengtai District.
entries.东湖渠#bc02cfe08cb2: "Geographical Names of Chaoyang District, Beijing" contains: East Lake Qu Village "Cheng Cun Yu Ming Dynasty. In the 21st year of Wanli Ming Dynasty (1593), the name of Donghuqu Village was first seen. At that time, it belonged to Daxing County. It was named because it was located east of Huqu Village (now North Huqu) in the Yuan Dynasty." "Chaoyang Historical Tale" says: Huqu Village became a village in Yuan Yanyou for three years (1316). Because it is located on the north bank of the North Xiaohe, the old low-lying terrain, every rainy season, the river is flooded, forming lakes and ditches, hence the name of Huqu Village. The village is adjacent to Baijia Village in the east, Shijia Village in the west, the small river in the south is adjacent to Houjiazhuang, and Dalizhuang in the north. The village has an irregular polygon.
entries.东四#b192d3478ef0: Since the Yuan Dynasty, the Eastern Fourth Area has been a relatively prosperous commercial area in the Metropolitan City. At that time, it was called the "Old Privy Council Corner City", commonly known as "Cross Street", which belonged to the Bright Lighting Workshop. In the Ming Dynasty, at the intersection of Chaoyangmen Inner Street and Chongwenmen Inner Street, four four four-pillar three-floor cross-street wooden plaques were built, respectively called "Sichengfang", "Renshoufang", "Baodaifang" and "Mingzhaofang", and two plaques at the south and north intersections were called "Dashijie Street", the east intersection was called "Shuren", and the west intersection was called "Xingyi". This place was called "Four Plaques".
entries.东四十条#e7e91e04d0e5: The "East Fourth" was called "Cross Street" in the Yuan Dynasty. In the Ming Dynasty, a four-poster, three-floor wooden plaque building was built on each side of the intersection. Because it was located east of the Imperial City, it was called "East Fourth" and referred to as "East Fourth" for short. It has long since disappeared, and "Dongsi" is still used as a place name today. From Dongsibei Street to Dongzhimen South Street on the east side, and from Chaoyangmen North Street to Dongzhimen South Street on the west side, there are 14 east-west alleys lined from south to north. The east fortieth alley is the tenth alley arranged from south to north, not the "40th alley in the east".
entries.东夏园#ce17fddf7337: According to legend, this place was once the vegetable garden of Prince Sue Haug, the first son of the Emperor Taichi of the Qing Dynasty and one of the "Eight Great Iron Hat Kings", and was originally a "fiefdom" given by the Imperial Court to imperial relatives. Because it was far from the capital city, Prince Su could not take care of it, so he was cultivated by several families of deserters, and symbolically handed over some silver coins to the Suwang Palace every year. In the first month of the third year of Shunzhi (1646), Prince Su was appointed as General Jingyuan to march to Sichuan, and in December of the same year, the regime of Zhang Xianzhong was defeated. In the fifth year of Shunzhi (1648), he returned to Beijing triumphantly in February, but in March, he was cut off by the Dorje structure. Afterwards, he was imprisoned and died in prison in April of the same year.
entries.东直门#d9e145408a73: In the Yuan, Ming and Qing Dynasties, most of the building materials needed for Beijing City entered from this gate. First, there were many brick kilns outside the Dongzhimen. Second, most of the blue bricks shipped from Shandong and the timber shipped from the southern provinces were transported to Tongzhou through the Beijing-Hangzhou Grand Canal, and then sent to the Dongzhimen by horse-drawn carriage. Therefore, the door is called "material door" and "brick and tile door". Also because the goods in the Wengcheng Commercial Stack are mainly daily necessities of suburban vendors, it is called "poor door". Dongzhimen Station is located in the northeast of Dongcheng District, at the intersection of Dongzhimen Inner Street, Dongzhimen Wai Street and Dong Erhuan Road, and can be interchanged with Line 13 and the Capital Airport Line.
entries.动物园#a2ae8a931e61: The history of the Beijing Zoo dates back to the 32nd year of the Qing Dynasty (1906), when it was known as "Wanshiyuan". Its predecessor was the Agricultural Experiment Site of the Ministry of Agriculture, Industry and Commerce of the Qing Dynasty. It integrates crop planting experiments and animal breeding. It has a park nature and was built on the former sites of Lok Sin Garden, Ji Yuan, Guang Sin Temple and Hui An Temple. In June 1908, the agricultural test site was completed and opened to visitors. The first animals on display were some of the animals purchased by the governor of the two rivers from Germany and some of the animals that the governor sent to the Qing Dynasty government from all over the country, about 100 species.
entries.垡头#cc2e4d3a5204: "Geographical Names of Chaoyang District, Beijing" contains: "Ming has become a village, Zeng Dezhuang. In the 21st year of Ming Wanli (1593), the name of Yantou Village was first seen. Due to the heavy texture of the soil, it is easy to unearth when cultivating, so it is called Yantou. Before 1949, it was originally two natural villages, former Yantou and later Yantou. In the early 1950s, large enterprises such as Beijing Coking Plant and Beijing Glass Factory were built here, and a large amount of land was expropriated. The two villages were merged, so it was called" today's name ".
entries.方庄#2ffc0e340797: Nowadays, the Fangzhuang is only a generic term, involving more than a dozen villages such as Fangjiazhuang, Puzhuang, Huangtukeng, Elm Village, Jiaojia Garden, Xiaoxinzhuang, Highland Village, Yanjialou, Kangjia Homeland, Longxi Temple, West Malaysia Huidian, East Malaysia Huidian, etc. in the 1970s. These villages are very small, even a few households. Among them, Fangjiazhuang is the largest, commonly known as "Fangzhuang". According to the "Fengtai Historical Tale", Fangzhuang was first called Fangjia Tomb, and the people of Mingde County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang Province, Congzhe Lizu. Fang Congzhe became a scholar in the 21st year of Ming Wanli (1593), and once held the position of Shangshu Libu and a bachelor at Dongge University.
entries.房山城关#53f27d5997d4: The station is named after the old site of Beichengguan, which is located in the historical Fangshan City North Pass. Chengguan is a common place name in China. It has a considerable relationship with the military, political, and economic of ancient cities and towns, and is basically divided based on military areas. At the end of the Qing Dynasty to the Republic of China, the important military facilities in each county were called "towns", and each city had checkpoints, and the checkpoints in the city were called "city passes". After 1949, most counties and cities established townships and towns (communes), and most of them were unrelated to cities, and the same was true of Fangshan City Pass.
entries.分钟寺#41532f294964: The "Geographical Names of Fengtai District, Beijing" is recorded as "Fenzhong Temple", which is called "the original temple name ‘Powder Temple’". entries.泥洼#687084acb2a5: The 泥洼 station area is documented in *Beijing Metro Station Names: Historical Notes*. This stop is associated with place-name history and local heritage along the line (source gist: 该站因南临前泥洼村，初设地铁站时称“前泥洼站”，后车站位置略有调整，大致处于前泥洼村与后泥洼村之间，故称“泥洼站”。公示地铁站名时曾有人提出“泥洼”之名太土气，…).
